When I finally moved on from my first job I thought things were going to get so much better. But instead of being bullied by customers I was bullied by supervisors. I’d leave for school at 530 in the morning and get back at 9 at night. I was exhuasted.
Trying to balance school and work drained the life out of me. I was working and schooling 7 days and getting a single day off was a joke. Then I got super sick and fell into an even greater shit pit.

I was constantly frowned upon because I wouldn’t take extra shifts. I made excuses to get out of working Saturdays because 6 days was too much for me. Then with a leadership change I was so optimistic things were going to be great.
Things got worse and the kids got violent. I was so worried about getting hit in the stomach constantly after two close calls at 20 weeks pregnant. The day the kids had a shoe fight I walked out.

As weeks went down and school died down I began to find myself. Began to understand myself. Began to know who I am. For the first time in 23 years I felt like this body I’d been stuck in for so long actually had a purpose.

And it was all because I decided to walk out of my job. Because I didn’t stress looking for more employment. Because I’m actually able to breath and look forward to a life break for an entire month. No one is on my back. No one is cutting me down.

I went from being unsure if I wanted to continue my education to deciding to take a route I otherwise would have never imagined myself in. I went from dreading going back to work to wanting to go back in the near future.
I’ve discovered talents I didn’t know I was capable of. Rediscovered old passions that had all but disappeared. I finally have an idea of what I want to do with my life.

I needed time to realize what I was capable of, what I loved, who I wanted to be. Since walking out of my job 10 weeks ago I’ve become a completely different person. One, for the first time in my life, I could be proud of.

Little did I know that walking out of my job was what I needed. That the weeks I spent pissed off at my past, angry at the present, and giving the middle finger to the future was EXACTLY what I’ve been needing forever.
